title: EFC Weak Lensing Phenomenology: A Testable μ(k,z) Framework and DES Y6 Validation Protocol
abstract_short: Testable μ(k,z) framework for weak lensing. Addresses S₈ tension (0.789 vs 0.83). Pass/fail criteria defined for DES Y6.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first dedicated weak-lensing phenomenology for EFC by deriving the scale- and redshift-dependent gravitational slip function μ(k,z) from Postulate A and building a concrete DES Y6 validation protocol. It directly addresses the S₈ tension as a natural EFC observable, provides a testable prediction pipeline for Stage-IV weak-lensing surveys, and bridges the gap between EFC's modified-gravity structure and real cosmic-shear data. This is the missing lensing channel that connects EFC's growth-rate predictions to photometric survey observables.
graph_insights: No prior papers in the graph touch weak lensing or μ(k,z); this paper creates a new node cluster that will connect to EFCLASS (when completed), to the S₈ tension literature, and to Postulate A — making it a bridge node between EFC's theoretical core and photometric survey phenomenology.

The absence of related papers at 1–2 hops confirms this is genuinely new territory for the EFC knowledge graph; the DES Y6 validation protocol node will become a high-betweenness node once survey data arrive.
The paper's coupling to Postulate A means any future revision of Postulate A propagates directly to the μ(k,z) functional form — this should be flagged as a dependency edge in the graph.

tests_added.name: DES Y6 μ(k,z) weak-lensing validation
tests_added.description: End-to-end pipeline comparing EFC-predicted μ(k,z) shear power spectrum against DES Y6 cosmic-shear two-point functions to test whether the S₈ tension is absorbed by EFC's modified gravitational slip.
tests_added.prediction: EFC μ(k,z) predicts a scale-dependent suppression of the lensing power spectrum at z < 1 that lowers the inferred S₈ relative to ΛCDM, resolving or substantially reducing the S₈ tension.

tests_added.name: S₈ tension absorption consistency check
tests_added.description: Verify that the EFC-predicted S₈ shift from μ(k,z) is consistent with the magnitude and direction of the S₈ tension reported by DES Y3, KiDS-1000, and HSC-Y3.
tests_added.data_source: DES Y3, KiDS-1000, HSC-Y3 published S₈ posteriors
tests_added.prediction: EFC's μ(k,z) generically shifts S₈ downward relative to Planck ΛCDM by 1–3σ, consistent with current lensing survey results.

tests_added.name: Scale-dependent μ(k,z) signature in shear correlation functions
tests_added.description: Test whether EFC's predicted k-dependent departure from GR μ=1 is detectable in the ratio of small-scale to large-scale shear correlation functions.
tests_added.prediction: EFC predicts a characteristic k-dependent tilt in μ(k,z) that produces a measurable scale-dependent ratio distinct from constant-μ modified-gravity models.

language_hedges.raw_claim: μ(k,z) framework resolves the S₈ tension
language_hedges.hedged_version: The EFC μ(k,z) framework predicts a shift in the inferred S₈ that is consistent in direction and magnitude with the observed S₈ tension; whether it fully resolves the tension requires DES Y6 / Rubin LSST validation.
language_hedges.reason: No empirical validation has been performed yet; the paper builds a protocol but does not execute it against released data. 'Resolves' overstates what is currently a structural prediction.

language_hedges.raw_claim: Testable μ(k,z) framework derived from Postulate A
language_hedges.hedged_version: A μ(k,z) weak-lensing phenomenology is constructed under the assumptions of Postulate A; its testability is contingent on the DES Y6 validation protocol being executed and the EFC Boltzmann solver (EFCLASS) being completed for full numerical forecasts.
language_hedges.reason: Without EFCLASS the numerical precision of the μ(k,z) predictions remains approximate; the paper derives the functional form but full forecasts await the Boltzmann solver. This is a structural prediction, not a closed proof.

language_hedges.hedged_version: A DES Y6 validation protocol is defined and ready for deployment once Y6 data products are publicly released; no blinding-stage or internal DES comparison has been performed.
language_hedges.reason: Protocol is designed but not yet executed; describing it as 'validation' without the qualifier 'protocol' could be mistaken for a completed validation.

new_hierarchy: 1. f σ₈(z) growth-rate measurements via DESI DR2 RSD (sealed prediction 32013156) — direct kinematic observable, most robust
2. CMB lensing × galaxy cross-correlation consistency (KC3/KC4 channel) — observational, independent of galaxy bias model
3. μ(k,z) weak-lensing shear power spectrum (this paper, 31188193) — structural signature in Stage-IV lensing surveys, awaiting DES Y6
4. kSZ velocity field signature (phenomenology-kSZ-velocity gap) — planned but no prediction paper yet
5. Early-structure JWST excess (phenomenology-jwst-early-structure gap) — qualitative, point prediction fragile until EFCLASS delivers quantitative forecasts

primary_discriminator_shift.old: f σ₈(z) growth rate from RSD remains the primary discriminator
primary_discriminator_shift.new: f σ₈(z) growth rate from RSD remains primary, but μ(k,z) weak-lensing now becomes the secondary independent channel
primary_discriminator_shift.reason: The weak-lensing μ(k,z) framework provides a geometrically independent observable channel (photometric lensing vs. spectroscopic RSD), strengthening the discriminator portfolio without displacing the kinematic growth-rate prediction.

ledger_impact.narrative_frame_reason: The paper does not close a kill criterion or restructure existing results, but it clarifies how EFC's μ(k,z) maps onto weak-lensing observables and provides the protocol by which DES Y6 data will test EFC, converting a qualitative expectation into a quantitative validation pipeline.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_sentence: EFC now has an explicit μ(k,z) weak-lensing framework derived from Postulate A, with a DES Y6 validation protocol ready for deployment once Y6 data are public.
implicit_consequences: The S₈ tension becomes a natural EFC validation target rather than merely a qualitative talking point; future S₈ measurements from any lensing survey can now be compared against the μ(k,z) prediction.
EFCLASS development priority increases because the μ(k,z) paper's quantitative C_ℓ forecasts are blocked until the Boltzmann solver is operational.

A combined RSD + weak-lensing joint analysis becomes possible once both DESI DR2 RSD and DES Y6 lensing data are available, providing a two-channel consistency test that is extremely difficult for ΛCDM extensions to mimic simultaneously.

The neutrino mass degeneracy gap (theory-neutrino-mass-degeneracy) gains new relevance because massive neutrinos also suppress lensing power; disentangling EFC μ(k,z) from neutrino-mass effects in lensing will require the degeneracy analysis.
Rubin LSST Y1 becomes a second independent validation target for the same μ(k,z) framework, extending the protocol beyond DES Y6.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline remains the biggest gap, but the weak-lensing μ(k,z) paper (31188193) adds a second urgent pipeline need: a DES Y6 cosmic-shear rapid-response module. Both sealed-prediction verification scripts should be assembled in parallel. EFCLASS completion is now upstream-critical for both channels.
